PullRequest.Title: chat: refine Agents handoff experiments and entry point telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Make Agents window entry-point attribution unambiguous and allow experiments to tune the current-chat handoff prompt.

| Entry point | Previous source | New source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current-chat handoff tip | `chatHandoff` | `currentChatHandoff` |
| Parallel-work invitation | `banner` | `parallelWorkEmptyChatHandoff` |
| Welcome: Try out the new Agents window | `banner` | `welcomeTryOut` |
| Welcome: View All Sessions | `banner` | `welcomeViewAll` |

- Add direct assignment-service treatments `chatAgentsHandoffTipTitle` and `chatAgentsHandoffTipDescription`, with independent localized fallbacks. No settings are added for copy.
- Add the advanced, experiment-configurable `chat.agentsHandoffTip.delaySeconds` setting (default: **5 seconds**). Show the tip only after that delay from the latest user message, including queued follow-ups, while the session remains in progress.
- Recalculate timing on new messages, focus changes, and configuration updates; safely handle treatment refreshes, dismissal, and disposal.

## Compatibility

- The handoff mode still defaults to `hidden`; existing per-window dismissal and persistent mute behavior are preserved.
- The separate no-folder notice remains immediate.
- Only window-open source values change; `agentsBanner.clicked` keeps its existing source values. Historical telemetry retains the old source names.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` (0 errors)
- Five focused unit suites covering handoff timing/copy, invitation ownership, launch actions, Welcome banners, and window-open telemetry: **171 passing**
- Targeted ESLint across all eight changed files
- `git diff --check`

Based directly on `release/1.139`, with no unrelated main-branch commits.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench eventually initializes the current-chat handoff and parallel-work contributions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Both contributions are created in WorkbenchPhase.Eventually, after restore; their treatment reads are asynchronous and do not block workbench restore or chat interaction because localized fallback copy remains usable while reads resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the shared experimentation assignment bundle through the main-process request service during TAS client initialization/refetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One service-level initial fetch (and one per service refetch), shared across all treatment names; the diff adds two logical value reads but not two independent network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assignment service already initialized/fetched globally, and the adjacent parallel-work contribution already read two treatments. The diff adds two local consumers for handoff copy without changing shared network-fetch cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the restore and chat critical paths: contribution initialization launches reads without awaiting them, and fallback copy is available immediately.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed four treatment names across the two singleton contributions: two pre-existing parallel-work names and two newly added current-chat handoff names; cardinality does not depend on chats, sessions, messages, or widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each contribution reads its title and description in one Promise.all. Assignment refreshes can overlap, but a monotonically increasing request id drops stale completions. The assignment service owns one shared TAS client and assignment-bundle fetch rather than issuing one network request per treatment.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a warm assignment cache, treatment values are read from the initialized TAS client. During cold initialization, all reads await the same client and prefer cached treatment variables until its single shared initial fetch completes; assignment refetches replace values and trigger bounded rereads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution phase, Promise.all cardinality, stale-request suppression, and the shared assignment-client initialization path are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact TAS initialization latency and refresh frequency vary by account/network, but they do not increase with message or session count and do not block the touched user workflows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added eager work is fixed-cardinality, eventually scheduled, cache-backed, and off the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user sends or queues messages in an eligible running Copilot CLI/agent-host chat and the handoff tip appears after the configured delay
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On request start, queue changes, focus changes, or relevant configuration changes, the contribution computes the latest user-message timestamp and arms one timeout. No filesystem, IPC, database, subprocess, or network operation is required before the tip can appear; expiration performs an in-memory notification update/render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The latest completed request is found by a reverse search and pending requests are scanned once per relevant lifecycle event. Effective cardinality is the focused chat's history tail plus its usually small pending queue, not all sessions or all widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A MutableDisposable owns exactly one timeout. Every reevaluation clears the previous timeout before arming another; focus changes replace model listeners through autorun reader-owned disposal. Queued follow-ups therefore move, rather than multiply, the deadline.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache is involved. The focused model and notification state are read in memory; `_lastPostedFor` plus copy fields suppress duplicate notification posts after the deadline.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the model's outer onDidChange emits request-structure events, while response fragments update the response model separately; timer replacement and listener disposal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long histories containing many trailing system-initiated requests could make the reverse search longer, but the event frequency is lifecycle-level rather than per streamed token and the pending queue is bounded by realistic user interaction; evidence does not establish material latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Work is bounded to one focused model, one timer, and sparse request/queue lifecycle events, with correct cancellation and deduplication.

Scenarios.Scenario: The tip or Welcome/parallel-work affordance opens the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click dispatches the existing open-session/open-workspace command and then follows the existing Agents-window creation path. Window opening remains the user-visible critical path; this diff only supplies more specific source enum values and preserves one dispatch per click.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the existing command that opens or focuses the Agents window and transfers the selected workspace/session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing open command per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same click issued the same open command once, using `chatHandoff` or `banner`; the PR changes only source attribution to `currentChatHandoff` or `parallelWorkEmptyChatHandoff`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing window-open IPC/process work is on the click critical path, but the diff does not add another call or move it earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the existing workspace-open command from a Welcome banner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one command dispatch per button click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The banner already dispatched one open command with source `banner`; it now chooses one of two source labels without changing boundary count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing Agents-window opening remains on the click critical path; source selection is an in-memory conditional.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One command and one window-open operation per explicit user click; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-driven, one invocation per click. The changed code adds no queue, burst, loop, or parallel window creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior. Existing workspace/session handoff state and telemetry handling are unchanged apart from the source label.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunks alter enum values and arguments while retaining the same command calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agents-window startup cost varies by machine and workspace, but no changed mechanism increases that cost, call count, serialization size, or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Telemetry/source refinement does not change expensive-boundary cardinality or scheduling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced initialization, delayed handoff scheduling, notification lifecycle, treatment fetching, and Agents-window open paths. No high-confidence, actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not provide sufficient evidence of fixing a prior shipped performance regression.
